meta.title: Japan Monetary & Liquidity Conditions Tracker
meta.framework: Monetary conditions (rates, money & credit, FX, balance sheet) and liquidity conditions (central-bank, funding, market)
meta.data_mode: LIVE (official sources) + SEED fallback for un-fetched series
meta.score_window: Each indicator is z-scored over its longest available history (polarity-signed so + = easier / more liquid); axes are weighted means of members; MCI / LCI are equal-weight means of their axes; the combined MLCI averages the two.
meta.source_note: Live where mapped (FRED mirrors of BoJ/BIS series); BoJ-only series (money-market spreads, JGB market functioning, balance-sheet shares) are illustrative seed anchored to recent observations until BoJ CSVs are ingested.

headline.assessment: Monetary conditions score +0.46 (mildly accommodative) and liquidity conditions -0.17 (mildly restrictive); the combined index is +0.14 (broadly neutral), each measured against the longest available history of its indicators (+ = easier / more liquid). Money growth is subdued (M2 +2.2% y/y) and the BoJ balance sheet is contracting (-8.2% y/y; monetary base -13.1%), while the yen remains weak in real effective terms (REER 64, 2020=100) — the quantity of money is tightening even as the exchange-rate channel stays easy. Funding liquidity is orderly (3m TIBOR-OIS 0.19pp; USD/JPY basis -30bp) and JGB market functioning is recovering (DI -14) as the BoJ's JGB share falls to 49%.

axes.label: Real short-rate stance
axes.desc: Ex-post real policy and 1Y rates: the price of money.

axes.label: Money & credit aggregates
axes.desc: Quantity of money and credit; the 'money view' inflation signal.

axes.label: Exchange rate (MCI)
axes.desc: Real effective yen: weaker = easier (classic MCI channel).

axes.label: Central-bank liquidity
axes.desc: Base money and reserves (BoJ current-account balances).

axes.label: Funding liquidity
axes.desc: Cost/ease of bank funding: TONA control, TIBOR-OIS, dollar basis.

axes.label: Market liquidity
axes.desc: JGB market functioning, bid-ask, free float, realized yield volatility, super-long slope, equity volatility.

bank_lending_yoy.name: Bank Lending Outstanding (y/y %)
bank_lending_yoy.notes: Lending by domestic commercial banks (avg amounts outstanding) y/y. IR04 carries the interest rate on loans outstanding, not the amount, so this stays seeded with verified BoJ prints pinned until the amounts-outstanding database is identified.

boj_assets_yoy.name: BoJ Total Assets (y/y %)
boj_assets_yoy.notes: Balance-sheet stance: expansion (QQE) = easier; contraction (JGB-purchase taper from Aug-2024) = tighter.

boj_ca_yoy.name: BoJ Current Account Balances (y/y %)
boj_ca_yoy.notes: Reserves held at the BoJ (excess reserves). Growth = more system liquidity.

boj_jgb_share.name: BoJ Share of Outstanding JGBs (%)
boj_jgb_share.notes: Central-bank absorption of the market; higher share = thinner free float, worse market liquidity (polarity -1).

call_policy_spread.name: Overnight Call Rate minus Policy Target (pp)
call_policy_spread.notes: Funding liquidity / rate control: TONA trading above target signals reserve scarcity or funding stress (polarity -1).

jgb_10s30s.name: JGB 10s30s Curve Slope (30Y minus 10Y pp)
jgb_10s30s.notes: Super-long term premium / fiscal-risk gauge from MoF yields. Steeper = more term-premium stress in the super-long zone (polarity -1).

jgb_10y_vol.name: 10Y JGB Realized Volatility (12m std of monthly changes bp)
jgb_10y_vol.notes: Computed from MoF yields. Higher volatility = impaired market liquidity / term-premium stress (IMF GFSR Apr-2026; June-2025 taper slowdown trigger).

jgb_bid_ask.name: 10y JGB Bid-Ask Spread (normalized ticks)
jgb_bid_ask.notes: BoJ 'Liquidity Indicators in the JGB Markets' style measure. Wider = less liquid (polarity -1).

jgb_market_functioning_di.name: JGB Market Functioning DI (BoJ Bond Market Survey)
jgb_market_functioning_di.notes: Degree of bond-market functioning (high minus low; negative = impaired). Fell to -64 in Feb-2023 under YCC; recovering since exit.

jpy_basis_3m.name: USD/JPY 3m Cross-Currency Basis (bp)
jpy_basis_3m.notes: Dollar-funding cost for Japanese banks; more negative = scarcer dollar liquidity (polarity +1: less negative = easier).

m2_yoy.name: Money Stock M2 (y/y %)
m2_yoy.notes: Broad money growth (BoJ Money Stock). Faster growth = easier monetary conditions; a leading inflation signal in the 'money view'.

m3_yoy.name: Money Stock M3 (y/y %)
m3_yoy.notes: Broadest money aggregate growth (BoJ). Secondary to M2.

monetary_base_yoy.name: Monetary Base (y/y %)
monetary_base_yoy.notes: Central-bank liquidity: base money growth (BoJ). Negative since 2024 as the balance sheet shrinks.

nikkei_vi.name: Nikkei Volatility Index (%)
nikkei_vi.notes: Implied equity volatility; spikes coincide with liquidity withdrawal (polarity -1).

real_1y_xp.name: Real Interest Rate 1-Year (ex-post)
real_1y_xp.notes: Headline real 1y: nominal minus realized core CPI. Scored over longest history (1974+).

real_policy_rate_xp.name: Real Policy Rate (ex-post vs realized core CPI)
real_policy_rate_xp.notes: Monetary conditions: ex-post real policy rate (policy rate minus realized core CPI). Lower = easier. History from 2004.

reer.name: Real Effective Exchange Rate (BIS broad; 2020=100)
reer.notes: Classic MCI input. Higher REER = stronger yen = tighter monetary conditions (polarity -1).

tibor_ois_3m.name: 3m TIBOR minus OIS (pp)
tibor_ois_3m.notes: Bank unsecured funding premium. Wider = tighter funding liquidity.

usdjpy.name: USD/JPY Exchange Rate
usdjpy.notes: Higher USDJPY = weaker yen = more accommodative for exporters/profits.

policy_rate.name: Uncollateralized Overnight Call Rate (policy rate)
policy_rate.notes: Uncollateralized overnight call rate, monthly average (BoJ Data Search FM02): the market rate the Bank steers to its target, and the policy rate of BoJ Review 2026-E-4. Target was raised to 0.50% Jan-2025, 0.75% Dec-2025, 1.00% Jun-2026.

core_cpi_yoy.name: Core CPI (ex-fresh food) y/y
core_cpi_yoy.notes: MIC CPI core (ex-fresh food). Context for 2% target.
